result:
I found one real bug in `dparse.parser`: one bad line in a requirements file can make parsing take exponential time. This is a regex denial of service (ReDoS), and it matches CVE-2022-39280, which is the vulnerability this checkout is pinned to.

**What happens:** every `-i`, `--index-url` or `--extra-index-url` line goes to `Parser.parse_index_server`, which runs `URL_REGEX.findall` on it. The host and domain parts of that regex nest repeated patterns that can match the same text in many ways. When a hostname almost matches but then fails, the regex engine retries an exponential number of combinations. Each extra `a.1` doubles the time:

```python
parse("-i https://" + "a.1"*26 + "\nrequests==2.0", file_type=filetypes.requirements_txt)
```

| repeats | time |
|---|---|
| 20 | 0.1 s |
| 22 | 0.38 s |
| 24 | 1.5 s |
| 26 | 6.4 s |

An ~80-character line takes 6 seconds, and a slightly longer one effectively never finishes. Any tool that runs dparse on untrusted requirements files can be hung this way.

**How it was found:** a Hypothesis test checked that index-URL parsing stays fast on hostnames built from repeated short chunks. It hung, and a per-example alarm caught the input `'a.1' * 37 + ' '`. Six other property tests passed:
- pinned `name==version` lines round-trip into the right dependencies
- `--hash` values are extracted correctly
- the index server is extracted and gets a trailing `/`
- index-server parsing stays under 0.5 s on short random inputs
- `-r` paths resolve relative to the requirements file
- parsing arbitrary text never crashes

**Fix:** the report includes a patch that replaces the regex with a simple split on `=` and whitespace. I checked it by swapping the patched function in at runtime: a line with 1,000 repeats parses in 0.1 ms, and the index-server and requirements round-trip tests still pass with the patch.

Files are in `runs/dparse_r4`:
- `bug_report_dparse_parser_2026-10-06_02-28_a5u6.md`
- `tests/test_dparse_parser.py`
- `find_slow.py`
- `repro.py`
